description.fun: Dunsparce is based on the tsuchinoko, a stubby snake of Japanese folklore, and its tiny wings only lift it a little off the ground, though some scientists think they were once used to fly. When spotted, it drills into the earth tail-first, back into maze-like tunnels that it finds its way through by the smell of the dirt and happily shares with Diglett. Its name mixes 'dun' with 'sparse', for its rarity.
description.guide: A Normal-type Pokémon based on the tsuchinoko of Japanese folklore, with tiny wings and a drill-like tail it uses to burrow. It lives underground in maze-like nests. It evolves into Dudunsparce when levelled up knowing Hyper Drill.
description.tagline: A winged, drill-tailed folklore snake that just won't fly

branches.text: Dunsparce has a 1 in 100 chance of evolving into the rare Three-Segment Form of Dudunsparce instead of the usual Two-Segment Form. The Pokécology book says the number of segments is set by its genes.

description.fun: Dudunsparce is basically Dunsparce with an extra body segment, and its name, a stuttered Dunsparce, may also nod to 'redundant'. It bores nests over six miles long into bedrock and blasts intruders out with air from its long, narrow lungs, yet it will kindly carry a lost Pokémon back outside on its back.
description.guide: A Normal-type Pokémon introduced in Generation 9, the evolution of Dunsparce, with a longer, segmented body and a pair of wings on each segment. It digs very long nests in bedrock and drives intruders out with blasts of air. It has a Two-Segment Form and a rare Three-Segment Form.
description.tagline: Dunsparce again, only longer, and it digs for miles

description.fun: About one Dunsparce in a hundred evolves into this rare form, which has an extra body segment with three stripes and three-feathered wings. Stretched out like that, it's the tallest Normal-type Pokémon of all.

transitions.how: Level up, knowing Hyper Drill, 99% chance
